# Trigger catalogue — sprezzature-ux-laws

**Generated by `scripts/build_triggers.py`. Do not hand-edit.** A test asserts this file equals the generated output, so a phrase added here and nowhere else fails CI.

Applies / audits the canonical Laws of UX (30 laws) with `--fix` for four mechanical fixers.

## When this skill is the answer

**You are holding:** An interface somebody is complaining about the FEEL of.

A phrase list cannot generalise — the ways to ask are unbounded, and a user almost never names the tool. What is bounded is the kind of thing in front of them. Match that first; the phrases below confirm a match, they do not make one.

Said without naming a tool: "this page is overwhelming", "too many options", "I can never find the button", « c'est confus »

## When it is not

Not this one when: the defect is mechanical accessibility (sprezzature-accessibility), contrast (sprezzature-colors), or the screen has yet to be built (sprezzature-ui). The exhaustive trigger catalogue is in `references/triggers.md`.

## Every phrase that names this skill

- `design this screen using Hick / Fitts / Miller`
- `what does Peak-End say here`
- `is this onboarding fighting the Paradox of the Active User`
- `audit for Laws of UX`
- `is my nav too Hick-heavy`
- `check my form for Postel / Tesler`
- `too many choices / options`
- `cognitive load`
- `Doherty threshold`
- `reduce clutter`
- `this page is overwhelming`
